subject: Request: Conditional SLO waiver for Medidata eval model launch
messages:
From: Nora Patel <nora@medidata.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-01 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Request: trial launch & SLO flexibility for new eval model

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the quick onboarding call yesterday. We're excited to kick off the 30-day evaluation of Redwood's new experimental sequence model (v0.9-eval). As discussed, this model improves recall on long clinical notes but has a higher and less-predictable tail latency under bursty loads.

Medidata's internal deadline for the proof-of-concept is April 20. To avoid blocking the trial while both sides collect traffic patterns, we'd like to request a temporary SLO adjustment for this evaluation window in the EU region:

- Uptime: standard 99.95% is fine; we can accept a 2× grace window for transient node drains.
- P99 latency: allow a 1.8× variance from the published P99 for 30 days while we collect telemetry and exercise prefix caching.

Attached is a short scope doc (medidata-eval-scope.xlsx) and a one-page draft waiver we used previously. Can you confirm whether this conditional relaxation is feasible and what the approval path looks like?

Thanks,
Nora
Nora Patel
Platform Lead, Medidata Labs
[Attachment: medidata-eval-scope.xlsx (XLSX)]
[Attachment: draft-slo-waiver.pdf (PDF)]

Folks — forwarding Medidata's ask. They're starting a time-bound eval (30 days) in eu-west-1 and are requesting a temporary P99 slack and tolerance for a couple of transient node drains. Attachments in the original.

Can product/infra/legal give a quick read on risk and what we can offer? Key constraints:
- This is a preview model (v0.9-eval) not yet in our standard catalog.
- Medidata needs timeline certainty to hit their internal April 20 milestone.

Rishi: any known queue/memory/kv-cache behaviour that could cause long tails for this family of models?
Lauren: if we approve a time-boxed SLO change, what contract language / cover letter do you need?
Hannah: if we sign off, I'll need a short customer-facing note re: expected behaviour and mitigation steps.

Thanks — Grace
Grace O'Connor

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: trial launch & SLO flexibility for new eval model

Quick technical notes from infra:

- v0.9-eval uses an expanded KV cache prefetch strategy that helps recall but increases memory pressure during cold starts. In eu-west bursts that exceed typical prefix reuse, we can see P99 spikes roughly 1.5–2× baseline for up to 10–15 minutes while caches warm.
- Autoscaler reacts to sustained CPU/GPU utilization; short bursts can produce higher queue depth before scale kicks in.
- Mitigations we can offer immediately: smaller initial batch-size cap, priority queueing for trial account, and a conservative autoscale cooldown override for the trial pool.

Operational ask: if we approve a temporary P99 variance of up to 1.8× for 30 days, infra will provision a small dedicated trial pool (single AZ) with autoscale tweaks and KV prewarm hooks. That reduces blast radius but may increase unit cost; rough estimate +12–18% on tokens while trial is active.

I'll be out for a few hours this morning but can help implement the config changes once legal signs off.

—Rishi
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-03 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: trial launch & SLO flexibility for new eval model

Legal POV — we can support a time-limited operational tolerance but need three guardrails documented and acknowledged by Medidata before any approval: 

1) Scope: explicit trial model and region (v0.9-eval, eu-west-1) and time window (2027-04-05 to 2027-05-05).
2) Metrics and reporting: Medidata must accept automated telemetry export access during the trial (redacted as needed) and agree to weekly syncs.
3) Liability cap: any SLA credits tied to this trial are capped at fees paid for the trial period; no changes to our standard SLA outside that window.

If those are acceptable, I can put together a one-page cover letter and a short addendum to the evaluation order that references the draft-slo-waiver.pdf they sent. We should avoid language that waives long-term obligations.

I'll draft language and attach to the Drive link once ready.

—Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

- P99 variance: up to 1.8× baseline for transient spikes, with infra mitigation (dedicated trial pool, autoscale tweaks)
